state:
- CDK5–NUP98 selection remains weakly motivated despite correctly labeling it speculative. Directly test allele-dependent CDK5 activation and identify a disease-enriched phosphosite with a displacement mechanism; distinctness from S1–S4 alone establishes limited novelty.
- Decisive experiments depend on unvalidated tools, especially the live phosphosite sensor and phosphorylation-independent pore tether. Prioritize the executable phosphoproteomics/depletion/phospho-null/import experiments, then specify reagent-development gates and fallback assays.
- Matched assembly burden does not establish matched transport-factor sequestration, while recruited CDK5 may phosphorylate neighboring pore proteins. Measure transport-factor partitioning and neighboring phosphosites, and add an orthogonal site-specific perturbation before assigning sufficiency to NUP98 phosphorylation.
